sections.h2: What is North Little Rock, and how does it relate to Little Rock?
sections.html:
North Little Rock is a separate city in Pulaski County on the north side of the Arkansas River, across from Little Rock. It has a mayor-council government led by Mayor Terry Hartwick, and an eight-member council with two members from each of four wards.

The Census Bureau estimates 65,120 residents for 2025, up from 64,591 in 2020, and it is the seventh-most populous city in Arkansas. The city had 44,097 residents in 1950, 64,388 in 1980 and 60,433 in 2000, so the population has hovered in a narrow range for decades.

2020 measureNorth Little Rock
Households28,967

Vacant units11.8%

With nearly one unit in eight vacant in 2020, a seller here may compete with a fair number of empty houses and rental units.

sections.h2: Why was the city once called Argenta?
sections.html:
North Little Rock began as Argenta, a community founded on April 18, 1871. Little Rock annexed it as an eighth ward in 1890, and the community was incorporated as the town of North Little Rock on July 17, 1901.

The name has flipped more than once: by 1904 the Arkansas Supreme Court let the town annex what remained of the ward, it took the name Argenta again in 1906, and it went back to North Little Rock in October 1917. City Hall, built in 1914, still has plaques and ornamental features that refer to Argenta.

That history shows up in the housing. The Argenta Historic District sits downtown, and the Park Hill neighborhood contains its own historic district.

sections.h2: What drives the North Little Rock economy?
sections.html:
Railroads, healthcare, sports venues and shopping anchor the local economy. Union Pacific dedicated its $40 million Downing B. Jenks diesel locomotive repair shop at 800 Pike Avenue in 1984, and hundreds of Union Pacific employees transferred to North Little Rock in 1987. The city also hosts the headquarters of Rock Region Metro and the Arkansas Municipal League.

  • Healthcare: Baptist Health Medical Center in North Little Rock, Eugene J. Towbin Healthcare Center and Arkansas Surgical Hospital.
  • Entertainment: Simmons Bank Arena and Dickey-Stephens Park, home of the Arkansas Travelers baseball team.
  • Shopping: McCain Mall and Lakewood Village.

The city sits directly across the river from downtown Little Rock, so employers on both banks are within reach of most North Little Rock streets.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods make up North Little Rock?
sections.html:
North Little Rock includes the Argenta Historic District, Park Hill, Lakewood and Levy, along with Amboy, Arrowhead Manor, Baring Cross, Chimney Rock, Crystal Hill, Dark Hollow, Dixie, Indian Hills, Mid-City, Overbrook, Pike View, Rose City and Windsor Valley.

Each area has its own housing age and price pattern, so a buyer or cash purchaser looks at the street before the city. If you own in Park Hill or Argenta, historic standards come into play for exterior work. If you own in Amboy or Indian Hills, storm history is the main talking point.

sections.h2: What did the 2023 tornado do to North Little Rock?
sections.html:
The March 31, 2023 EF3 tornado crossed North Little Rock after starting in west Little Rock. It passed through Burns Park, Amboy and Indian Hills before reaching Sherwood and Jacksonville, and its peak winds were 165 mph.

The National Weather Service singled out Burns Park, where at least 10,000 trees were lost. Across the whole path, at least 2,700 structures were affected and about 60,000 power outages were reported. Severe thunderstorms are also most common in spring here, and the climate is humid subtropical with an average yearly temperature of 62.5 degrees.

If your North Little Rock house has storm-related repairs, keep receipts, permits and insurance paperwork together. Buyers and lenders both ask.

sections.h2: What historic rules apply in the Argenta Historic District?
sections.html:
Owners in the Argenta Historic District must get a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic District Commission before changing a structure's exterior. Regulated changes include room additions, doors, windows, awnings, porches and signs, and new construction and demolition also need review.

  • The commission meets on the second Thursday of each month at 6 p.m.
  • A public hearing notice is published two weeks before review, and adjacent owners are notified.
  • After approval, the owner gets a building permit from the city planning department, and there is no building permit fee within the district.
  • A denial can be appealed to the Pulaski County Circuit Court.
  • Commission office: 506 Main Street, 501-371-0755.

If you own an Argenta house, a buyer will want to know about any approved or pending exterior work. Anything unfinished should be sorted out or disclosed before closing.

sections.h2: How does North Little Rock handle nuisance structures?
sections.html:
The city council may condemn nuisance structures by resolution after a public hearing, and it is unlawful to own, keep or maintain a structure condemned by that resolution. The resolution must describe the structures, name the owners and make findings that they are unfit for occupancy or harmful to life, property or public safety.

Under the city's definitions, a nuisance structure can be dilapidated and unsafe, unsanitary enough to threaten health or safety, or a more than ordinary fire hazard. Unsafe structures include those at risk of partial or complete collapse. City Hall is at 300 Main Street and City Services is at 700 W 29th Street, both open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The city's page does not list a code enforcement phone number, so call city hall for details on any specific notice.

sections.h2: What roads, schools and airport serve North Little Rock?
sections.html:
Interstate 30 ends in North Little Rock, the Arkansas portion of Interstate 57 begins here, and Interstate 40, US 65, US 67 and US 167 run through the city. Rock Region Metro, the state's largest transit agency, runs Metro Rail streetcars through Argenta. North Little Rock Municipal Airport serves as a reliever airport for Clinton National.

Most students attend the North Little Rock School District, which has one high school, one middle school, nine elementary schools and an early childhood center. The Pulaski County Special School District runs several other area schools.

sections.h2: How are deeds, taxes and sales handled for a North Little Rock house?
sections.html:
A North Little Rock deed is recorded with the Pulaski Circuit and County Clerk, at 401 West Markham Street in Little Rock. Recording costs $15 for the first page and $5 for each added page, and the filing needs a transfer tax form. Since August 5, 2025, people filing a deed need a photo ID unless they are attorneys, brokers, financial institution representatives or government representatives.

The state's real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000. Arkansas counties collect property tax from the first business day of March through October 15 of the following year, with a 10 percent penalty on late payments. Homestead taxable value can rise no more than 5 percent a year, and a formal appeal must be scheduled with the county board of equalization by the third Monday in August.

You can list, sell on your own or accept a cash offer. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can be a fit for storm-damaged, inherited, vacant or tenant-occupied property, especially if a nuisance notice is on the horizon.

faqs.q: How many people live in North Little Rock?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 65,120 residents for 2025, after counting 64,591 in 2020.

faqs.q: Do historic district rules affect selling in Argenta?
faqs.a: They affect exterior work, not the act of selling. Owners need a Certificate of Appropriateness for changes like windows, doors, porches and additions, and buyers will ask about open approvals.

faqs.q: Was North Little Rock hit by the 2023 tornado?
faqs.a: Yes. The March 31, 2023 EF3 tornado passed through Burns Park, Amboy and Indian Hills. At least 10,000 trees were lost in Burns Park.

faqs.q: Which county handles North Little Rock deeds and property tax?
faqs.a: Pulaski County. Deeds are recorded at the Pulaski Circuit and County Clerk's Real Estate Department.

faqs.q: Can North Little Rock condemn my house?
faqs.a: Yes, the city council can condemn a nuisance structure by resolution after a public hearing, if it finds the building unfit for occupancy or harmful to public safety.

faqs.q: What is the state transfer tax on a deed?
faqs.a: $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on deeds over $100, according to the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration.
